commands.author: FMLS

target.title: docs(browser): expose batch/doubleClick/scrollIntoView/labels in tool schema and docs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The browser runtime already supports `batch`, `scrollIntoView`, `doubleClick`,
and `labels`/`annotations`, but an agent reading the `browser` tool schema, the
bundled `browser-automation` skill, or the public docs cannot discover them:
the schema fields carried no descriptions, the skill omitted `batch` and
`doubleClick` entirely, and `docs/tools/browser.md` only mentioned `batch` as an
existing-session limitation. As a result, models underuse `act:batch` (sending
individual round trips instead) and fall back to `evaluate` or coordinate
clicks instead of using `doubleClick` / `scrollIntoView`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discoverability finish-up for already-shipped runtime behavior (M0.2 in the
browser tool plan), not new functionality:

- Add `description` to `BrowserToolSchema` fields (`kind`, `actions`,
  `stopOnError`, `doubleClick`, `labels`) so an agent reading only the tool
  schema sees what each act kind/field does. `kind` now calls out `batch`
  (nested `actions[]`) and `scrollIntoView` explicitly.
- Extend the tool's top-level description with a one-line `batch` /
  `doubleClick` / `labels` summary.
- Document `batch`, `doubleClick`, and `scrollIntoView` as agent-usable in the
  `browser-automation` skill, `docs/tools/browser.md`, and
  `docs/tools/browser-control.md` (new "Act kinds and batch" section).

CLI exposure (`--double`, `scrollintoview`, `--labels`) was already complete
and is not changed. The `openclaw browser batch` CLI subcommand is
intentionally out of scope and tracked under M1.6, so `batch` remains
reachable through the agent tool / `act` for now.

## User Impact

Agents using the `browser` tool can now discover `act:batch`, `doubleClick`,
`scrollIntoView`, and `labels` from the tool schema and the bundled skill
without reading source or HTTP routes, reducing unnecessary round trips and
`evaluate` fallbacks. No runtime behavior, config, or CLI flag changes; users
who never read the schema/skill are unaffected.

## Evidence

HEAD: `64631d6e3f57d6e3667aa7c6800f931eac45581a`
Branch: `docs/browser-schema-discoverability` (fork: FMLS/openclaw)

### Live terminal capture (HEAD 64631d6e3f57d6e3667aa7c6800f931eac45581a)

Focused test for the changed surface (browser-tool schema + description),
verbose reporter. The three test groups below are the ones that exercise the
touched schema fields and the tool description contract; the full file run
reports `110 passed`:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 ✓ |extension-browser| extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts > browser tool description > warns agents about existing-session act timeout limits 12ms
 ✓ |extension-browser| extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts > browser tool act compatibility > sizes node proxy calls for recursively nested batch execution 1ms
 ✓ |extension-browser| extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts > browser tool snapshot labels > returns image + text when labels are requested 1ms
 ... (107 more passing, including browser tool act compatibility > accepts flattened act params for backward compatibility, browser tool act stale target recovery, browser tool external content wrapping)
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  110 passed (110)
   Duration  8.35s
```

The `browser tool description` test (extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts:490) still passes, confirming the new description sentence keeps the existing `action=profiles` / `omit timeoutMs on act:type` / `browser-automation skill` / `paths-only arming` contract assertions green and does not introduce the forbidden `profile="user"` literal.

### Whole-surface inspection

- Changed schema surface: `extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.schema.ts`. `BROWSER_ACT_KINDS` already lists `batch` (line 18) and `scrollIntoView` (line 24); `doubleClick`, `labels`, and `actions`/`stopOnError` were already exposed. This PR only adds `description` strings; no field/kind is added, removed, or re-typed, so the provider-schema shape (flattened object, no `anyOf`) and the OpenAI top-level `type: "object"` requirement (file header comment) are preserved.
- Tool description: `extensions/browser/src/browser-tool-description.ts`. The added line is a pure string append to the existing array; `describeBrowserTool` is called by both lazy registration and runtime execution (file header), so the agent-facing description and any cached tool registration stay in sync.
- Runtime callers/callees: no runtime code reads these descriptions; they are consumed only by provider tool-schema serialization. The act runtime (`agent.act.normalize.ts`, `pw-tools-core.interactions.ts` `batchViaPlaywright`) already implements `kind=batch` / `scrollIntoView` / `doubleClick` and is unchanged.
- Sibling tests: `extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts` covers `doubleClick` (line 2308), nested `batch` (line 2488-2503), and `labels` (line 2531-2561); all 110 tests pass.
- Docs/skill: `extensions/browser/skills/browser-automation/SKILL.md`, `docs/tools/browser.md`, and `docs/tools/browser-control.md` gain new sections/bullets only; no existing guidance is contradicted (the existing-session `batch` unsupported note is preserved and referenced from the new sections).

### Static checks

- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — passed (covers `extensions/**/*.ts` incl. both changed `.ts` files).
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.extensions.json extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.schema.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool-description.ts` — passed.
- `pnpm format extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.schema.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool-description.ts` (oxfmt) — no formatting changes needed; output already compliant.
- `markdownlint-cli2` on the 3 changed `.md` files — 0 issues.
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- `pnpm check:changed` attempted to delegate to Blacksmith Testbox but the local crabbox binary was unavailable; per root AGENTS.md ("remote backend unavailable → trusted-source falls back to local execution"), the focused test + tsgo + oxlint + markdownlint above were run locally to cover the changed surface.
